subject.title: Add OS-level resource caps to the existing exec budget primitive

question: Should the shared core exec runner own optional host OS resource enforcement for approved local jobs, or should resource isolation remain limited to sandbox and operator-managed execution layers?
rationale: The gap is real and vision-aligned, but adopting it creates a permanent cross-platform core and possible plugin-runtime contract whose ownership cannot be inferred from existing behavior.

options.title: Sponsor a core budget contract
options.body: Add a generic capability-reported budget at the runner/spawn boundary, initially backed by one well-proven Linux adapter with explicit unsupported results elsewhere.

options.title: Keep isolation outside exec
options.body: Leave the shared host primitive unchanged and direct resource-sensitive workloads through sandbox backends or operator-managed cgroups and service units.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core budget contract
recommendation.body: Add a generic capability-reported budget at the runner/spawn boundary, initially backed by one well-proven Linux adapter with explicit unsupported results elsewhere.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the documented overall product owner and the decision affects the shared core execution boundary rather than one isolated caller.
